paper.title_en: Suppressed Direct Detection of Dark Matter from a Non-Invertible Selection Rule
paper.abstract_en: Although the existence of dark matter is well established, its particle nature is still unknown. Direct detection experiments have been struggling to find any viable signal, implying that the dark matter--nucleon scattering cross-section must be suppressed. Here we propose a mechanism to explain the origin of this suppression by considering a non-invertible selection rule. Our numerical analysis shows that a suppressed yet predictable dark matter--nucleon scattering cross section is possible.
